elements.scope_reason: Red-box header is a trigger condition ('unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy') for a management action (give emergency contraception), not a diagnosis or an urgent-attention box. The language could express it as a check task / possible rule (SNOMED 'Unprotected sexual intercourse' finding exists; '< (onset ...) (time_ago 5 days)' is representable), and the house standard says red-box items become check tasks; but the page names no priority and no diagnosis, so reasonable people could leave it out.
parts_missing: unprotected sexual intercourse within past 5 days (e.g. clinical_finding 'Unprotected sexual intercourse' with onset < time_ago 5 days)

elements.problem: Nothing in the file relates to the red box; the only red box on the page is entirely unencoded. If the builders judged it management-only, that is defensible, but no trigger/check for recent unprotected sex exists, so the time-critical emergency-contraception pathway is invisible to the rules.

'if pregnancy suspected (nausea/breast tenderness/missed period when using combined oral contraceptive), check for pregnancy' is a 'suspect X' conclusion -> possible Pregnancy. The 'before starting contraception, check for pregnancy' half is a test/management step and out of scope.
elements.problem: Encoded as possible Pregnancy when on COC AND any of nausea / breast tenderness / missed period, with a matching check task; concepts exist and are appropriate ('Missed period' is the closest to the page wording). Minor: the page's parenthesis is ambiguous whether 'when using COC' qualifies all three signs or only 'missed period'; the rules apply it to all three, which is the more natural reading but narrows the rule (a woman on an injectable/implant or not yet on contraception with a missed period gets no possible-pregnancy rule here). 'Missed period' will not match a recorded 'Amenorrhea'/'Secondary amenorrhea' (not a descendant).
evidence: (task "Check for suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive") :: (task ... adult (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Uses combined oral contraception" "finding")) (check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Nausea" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tenderness of breast" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Missed period" "finding"))))

Diagnose possible pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Pregnancy" "finding") possible) adult (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Uses combined oral contraception" "finding")) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Nausea" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tenderness of breast" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Missed period" "finding"))))

rule_level_problems.problem: No rule addresses the page's only red box (emergency contraception after unprotected sex in the past 5 days). There is no check for 'Unprotected sexual intercourse' with a 5-day onset window, so a time-critical need is never surfaced by the rules. Defensible only if the whole box is treated as management.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive
rule_level_problems.problem: Restricts all three suspicion signs to COC users. A missed period in a patient not on COC (or about to start contraception — the page's other trigger for a pregnancy check) yields no possible-pregnancy rule on this page.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for suspected pregnancy on combined oral contraceptive / Diagnose possible pregnancy …
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Missed period' is not an ancestor of 'Amenorrhea'/'Secondary amenorrhea', so a clinician recording amenorrhoea would not trigger the rule; consistent between task and rule otherwise (every check_for item is used as evidence).

summary: The page's red box (emergency contraception within 5 days of unprotected sex) is not encoded at all; it is mostly management, but the trigger itself (recent unprotected sex) could have been a check/possible rule and is the most consequential omission. The only logic encoded — possible pregnancy on COC with nausea, breast tenderness or missed period — is correct with sound SNOMED concepts, though it narrows suspicion to COC users. Everything else on the page is management, cross-references or BMI (not representable).
